recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-37801 unless a future work-group decision changes Composition.subject cardinality again.
issue_request: FHIR-37801 was a Published/Persuasive R5 Structured Documents request to change Composition.subject to 0..* so regulatory documents, including product labels, can identify multiple subjects without List, Group, or Composition.section workarounds.
initial_application: The issue was applied before this reconciliation. Commit d0d4a77daa74ccb388177a1b07ee6709dd0fe1eb changed source/composition/structuredefinition-Composition.xml from max 1 to max *, and merge commit 373eff25e30352565cebf98de6aa209d89af481f brought the FHIR-37801 PR into the main history.
additional_context: Composition is active in source/fhir.ini. SD 2022-08-04 minutes corroborate the product-label rationale and 17-0-0 motion to accept the change. Earlier core issues relaxed the minimum cardinality, and a later Clinical Document IG issue acknowledged the R5/R6 multiple-subject behavior while leaving separate IG guidance unchanged.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/composition/structuredefinition-Composition.xml already defines Composition.subject with min 0 and max *. Editing current source would be redundant and could risk disturbing unrelated profile-specific constraints.
